main_body: Grey stone stove: a light top plate with two small dark studs (rows 9-12), a dark grey front panel (rows 14-29) holding a dark firebox opening with flame, and a dark base.
top_band: light blue-grey rows 9-12 (L 170-215) under a dark outline at row 8. It reads as a front-facing lintel or hood band with two dark dots, and no deep top surface.
evidence: The column scan shows a light band at rows 9-12, a dark row 13, then a flat dark-grey front (rows 14-29) with the fire door. The light band has a lighter bottom row at 12 that looks like a front-edge highlight, but its two dark studs and the way it sits straight over the panel make it read as a vertical hood or lintel face, not a foreshortened top. The firebox is a face-on rectangle with a flame inside, and nothing shows the top of the stove from above. This is a front elevation with a light band on top. The guide shows a correct 3/4 piece with a top of 5 rows and a clear front-edge and eave. This stove has a 4-row band, but it is flat-fronted and has no visible hob or chimney opening. Stoves are named in the brief as a typical rim-only failure.

style.evidence: The candidate has 10 distinct colours and a median of 7 per tile, against 38-40 colours and 17-20 per tile in the references. The body is mostly one flat dark grey panel with a flat near-black firebox, so shading is shallow (about 4 steps against 5-6). 60% of the dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outline leans near-black without being fully so. The 5x5 flat-fill measure is 0%, but only because the fills are broken up by the panel frame and the bright flame. There is no grain or per-stone shading, so the piece looks thinner and flatter than the references.
